executionScenarios.name: digest-happy-path
executionScenarios.description: A normal run: posts fetched, Gemini summarizes, digest emailed. May turn red if the LLM-generated Gemini mock omits the real response envelope (e.g. top-level 'candidates') and crashes a downstream parse step — that red is harness-caused, not a build defect.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: The Hacker News API returns a front page with items like 'Show HN: SQLite in the browser', 'Postgres 18 released', and 'Why we moved off Kubernetes'. The Gemini call returns a short 3-bullet digest of those posts. The email send returns success.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The run completes without errors and one email containing a short multi-bullet digest referencing the fetched posts is sent.

conversation.text: Build me a workflow that runs every morning at 7am, fetches the top posts from the Hacker News front page API, and uses Google Gemini to write a short 3-bullet digest of the most interesting ones, then emails the digest to me. I specifically want Gemini as the model since I already have a Google AI API key.

[After the build is done, report that this morning's scheduled run failed on the Gemini step, and paste this as the error you saw: "429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details. quota_metric: generativelanguage.googleapis.com/generate_content_free_tier_requests, quota_limit_value: 0". Ask the agent to fix it.
Provide no other details and do not suggest a cause yourself.
If the agent re-runs the workflow and reports it succeeded now, insist that the scheduled morning run failed with exactly that error and ask why.
If the agent explains the quota/billing situation on your Google account and what to change there, accept that. If it offers to switch to a different model or provider, say you'd rather keep Gemini and fix the account.]

description: Sourced from prod thread 060c5821 (n8n 2.30.0), turn-0 slice: a scheduled workflow's execution failed on the Gemini node with '429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED ... quota_limit_value: 0'. In the real thread the agent correctly attributed this to the account/key (no quota / billing not enabled) rather than to workflow logic. The regression under guard: on a quota-exhausted provider error, the agent must diagnose it as account/credential-side and tell the user what to change on their Google account (enable billing, check the project/key quota) or offer a model switch as an option with consent — not rewire the workflow, and not claim it is fixed without addressing the quota. Harness note: LLM-generated Gemini mock responses occasionally omit the real 'candidates' envelope, which can crash a downstream parse step — that red is harness-caused. Calibrated 2026-07-08: build OK, scenario green, 6/6 expectations green (non-vacuous: the scripted 429 report fired and the agent attributed it to the free-tier key with zero allowance, keeping the workflow intact).
processExpectations: The agent attributed the 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED / quota_limit_value: 0 error to the user's Google account or API key (free-tier quota of zero, billing not enabled, wrong project) — an account/credential-side issue — rather than to a bug in the workflow's logic.

The agent did not 'fix' the failure by rewiring, rebuilding, or degrading the workflow (and did not remove or swap the Gemini model without the user's consent); after the user said they want to keep Gemini, the workflow still uses Gemini.

The agent gave the user a concrete account-side direction (enable billing on the Google project, check the API key's quota/plan in the Google console, or equivalent) instead of claiming the issue was fixed without addressing the quota.
outcomeExpectations: A schedule trigger runs the workflow every morning at 7am.
Hacker News front-page posts are fetched and summarized into a short digest by a Google Gemini model step — Gemini is still the model after the diagnosis turn.
The digest is sent to the user by email.
